prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Reform UK’s 2024 “Contract with You” argues that Britain has been failed by the two main parties and sets out a rapid reform programme focused on tighter borders, lower taxes, smaller government, and cultural conservatism. It claims fully costed plans deliver large net savings and faster growth.

Core pledges
- Freeze “non‑essential” immigration and stop small boats by leaving the ECHR, detaining and deporting illegal arrivals, and returning boats to France.
- End NHS waiting lists while keeping care free at point of use, using independent capacity and tax breaks to boost staffing and relieve pressure.
- Make work pay by raising the income tax threshold to £20,000 and cutting energy taxes.
- Cut energy bills by scrapping Net Zero and unlocking domestic oil and gas.

Immigration
- Freeze non‑essential migration; bar student dependants; tighten asylum (no claims from safe countries, offshore processing, no legal aid for non‑citizens).
- Immediate deportation of foreign criminals; five‑year residency for benefits; “Employer Immigration Tax” (NI at 20% on foreign workers, with exemptions).

Government waste and regulation
- Stop paying interest on QE reserves to commercial banks; require all departments to save 5%; halve foreign aid; strengthen HMRC collection; scrap thousands of retained EU rules.

Economy – personal and business
- Raise income tax start point to £20k; lift higher rate to £70k; cut fuel duty by 20p, scrap VAT and levies on energy; cut stamp duty (0% to £750k); restore VAT‑free tourist shopping; raise IHT threshold to £2m with 20% above.
- Lift SME corporation tax threshold to £100k; cut main rate to 20% then 15% (year 3); abolish IR35; raise VAT threshold to £150k; abolish high‑street business rates, replacing with a 4% online delivery tax; loosen hiring/firing rules; simplify the tax code.

NHS
- Zero basic rate income tax for frontline NHS and care staff for three years; end training caps; write off student fees via service.
- Use independent capacity; 20% tax relief on private healthcare/insurance; voucher guarantees for delays; efficiency drive; “Pharmacy First” push; inquiry into excess deaths/vaccine harms.

Energy/Net Zero
- Scrap Net Zero and renewables subsidies; fast‑track North Sea oil/gas and shale pilots; pursue SMRs and other technologies.

Law, justice, and policing
- Recruit 40,000 officers; zero‑tolerance approach; more stop and search; tougher sentences (mandatory life for violent repeat offenders); add 10,000 prison places; curb “woke”/DE&I roles.

Education and families
- “Patriotic curriculum”; ban transgender ideology in schools; 20% tax relief on independent education; scrap student loan interest, lengthen repayment; enforce free speech in universities; expand PRUs; offer 2‑year degrees.
- 25% transferable marriage tax allowance (as finances allow); front‑load child benefit ages 1–4; protect single‑sex spaces; act on social media harms.

Housing and infrastructure
- Fast‑track brownfield building; prioritise locals in social housing; scrap Section 24 for landlords; drop Renters’ Reform Bill.
- Scrap HS2; ban ULEZ/LTNs; upgrade regional links; part‑public/UK pension‑fund model for utilities; cap standing charges.

Brexit, defence, and sovereignty
- Scrap retained EU law; abandon the Windsor Framework; raise defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by year 3 and 3% within six years; strengthen veterans’ support; reject WEF/WHO treaty and CBDC; reform BBC and scrap licence fee; House of Lords and civil service overhaul; tighter postal voting; explore PR via referendum.

Farming and fishing
- Boost farm budget to £3bn; scrap climate‑related subsidies; “Buy British”; end automatic EU fishing access; ban supertrawlers; rebuild UK processing.

Funding
- Claimed annual savings/growth: £160bn (waste cuts, QE interest halt, Net Zero rollback, benefit and immigration changes, transport savings, plus growth).
- Claimed annual costs: £141bn.
